title: Topic Coherence Embedding Audit Protocol
content:
Purpose:
This doc defines an actionable protocol for auditing topic-level coherence and semantic relevance for new embedding models during onboarding. It combines semantic-search-style relevance judgments with manual cluster-coherence sanity checks across domains and languages. The goal is to provide an interpretable pass/fail gating signal plus a lightweight diagnostic report to guide model selection or tuning (quantization, pooling, normalization).

Scope and motivation:
- Target: embedding vectors used for semantic search, intent clustering, and topic grouping across product content, help docs, support tickets, and multilingual user queries.
- Why separate topic coherence from pairwise similarity: a model can have high pairwise retrieval metrics yet produce semantically inconsistent clusters (topic drift inside clusters), which hurts downstream UX (bad facets, noisy reranks).
- This protocol is intended for: new open model checkpoints, quantized variants, and candidate finetune variants.

High-level acceptance criteria (pass/fail):
- Semantic search: NDCG@10 >= 0.68 on the cross-domain relevance set OR relative improvement over baseline >= 3% if baseline is recent.
- Clustering coherence: average human cluster coherence rating >= 3.5/5 across sampled clusters and cluster purity >= 0.7 for k chosen by elbow heuristic.
- Multilingual parity: degradation vs English baseline <= 10% on NDCG@10 for high-resource languages (es, fr) and <= 20% for lower-resource languages (hi, vi).
If any threshold fails, the model is flagged for remediation and a diagnostics runbook is produced.

Dataset construction rules (sampling and composition):
1) Domains: sample from four domains to capture different topical structures: product-FAQ (short Q/A), developer docs (medium-form technical), customer support (short-to-medium conversational), and marketing/blog (long-form topical). Aim for 2,000 canonical passages per domain.
2) Query sets:
   - Semantic search relevance: 800 queries stratified by domain (200 per domain). Each query paired with 50 candidate passages (mix of true positives, near-miss negatives, and random negatives).
   - Clustering sanity: sample 2000 unlabeled passages aggregated across domains. For human labeling, we create cluster buckets by running k-means with multiple k and then annotate 50 clusters (approx 10–50 items each) per model for human coherence scoring.
3) Multilingual: for language parity, include paraphrase and translation pairs. Collect source English content where possible and native-language documents for es, fr, hi, vi. For lower-resource languages include ~500 passages each. Use translation/back-translation only as augmentation when native data is sparse.

Embedding extraction configuration (to record precisely):
- Model checkpoint tag (e.g., model-name@sha256)
- Tokenization scheme and library + version
- Pooling method: CLS, mean of last layer, mean of last-4-layers, weighted mean
- Postprocessing: L2-normalize? yes/no, PCA dim reduction (if used), quantization details
Record all of these for every run; differences in pooling/normalize often explain large metric shifts.

Annotation protocol: semantic relevance (relevance judgments)
- Labelers: in-house annotators with domain primers + short training session (30–45m).
- Relevance scale: 0 (irrelevant), 1 (marginally related), 2 (relevant), 3 (highly relevant).
- Guidance: "relevant" means the passage would satisfy the user query in a single-turn search. "Marginal" includes partial answers or tangentially related content.
- QC: 10% overlap between annotators to compute inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff alpha target >= 0.75).

Annotation protocol: cluster coherence (sanity checks)
- For each sampled cluster: show annotators the full text of cluster members and ask:
   1) Does this cluster represent a single coherent topic? (Yes/No)
   2) Rate coherence 1–5 where 5 = all items clearly about the same narrowly-defined topic, 1 = items are unrelated.
   3) List up to three brief tags that best describe the cluster (free text).
- Provide examples of coherent vs incoherent clusters in the primer.
- Use 3 annotators per cluster, take majority for Yes/No and average for coherence score.

Automatic metrics to compute (and rationale):
- Retrieval: MRR, NDCG@10, Recall@50, Precision@10. NDCG is primary because graded relevance is used.
- Clustering: silhouette score (embedding-space), Davies-Bouldin index, cluster purity (using human tags as labels), and average human coherence rating.
- Topic-level drift detection: for clusters that have high silhouette but low human coherence, compute TF-IDF topic distance between cluster centroid and members to surface lexical vs semantic divergences.
- Multilingual parity: compute per-language NDCG@10 and normalized degradation vs English.

Evaluation pipeline steps (automated + human):
1) Run embedding extractor for candidate model across the full dataset and persist vectors with metadata (doc id, domain, lang, token_count, pooling).
2) Automated retrieval metrics: compute recall and NDCG using offline candidate sets.
3) Automated clustering runs: run k-means for k in {20, 50, 100} and compute silhouette / DB-index. Save cluster assignments for manual sample selection.
4) Sample clusters and queries for human annotation. Create annotation batches with overlap for QC. Push to annotation queue (internal tool).
5) When human labels return, compute human-driven metrics (coherence average, cluster purity, inter-annotator agreement).
6) Combine signals into diagnostic report and checklist: pass/fail flags, top 5 failure modes, recommended next steps (tune pooling, add L2 norm, change quantization).

Failure modes and common remedies (empirical notes):
- High retrieval, low cluster coherence: model captures topical similarity for short queries but fails to preserve fine-grained topical boundaries. Remedy: try last-4-layers weighted mean or retrain with contrastive examples encouraging cluster separation.
- Low multilingual parity: tokenization mismatch or model not exposed to language; try cased tokenization, language-specific pooling, or filter training data. Consider translation augmentation for low-resource languages.
- High silhouette but low human score: lexical similarity dominates embedding space; use semantic-rich contrastive fine-tuning or reduce reliance on TF-IDF-derived negatives during pretraining.

Reporting template (what to include in the onboarding ticket):
- Run metadata (model tag, pooling, normalization, run date)
- Summary table: NDCG@10 overall, per-domain, per-language; MRR; cluster purity; avg coherence; silhouette
- Top failure clusters (include 3–5 cluster examples with member excerpts and annotator comments)
- Recommended quick experiments (e.g., switch to mean-last-4, enable L2-normalize, re-run with augmented negatives)
- Decision: Accept / Reject / Needs follow-up experiments

Quick sample prompts and query examples (do not share externally):
- Product FAQ (EN): "How do I reset API keys for an account?" Candidate passages should include step-by-step instructions or settings page pointers.
- Developer doc (EN): "What is the recommended way to cache KV caches between requests?" Relevant passages: runtime caching, kv eviction, serialization notes.
- Support ticket (ES): "No puedo iniciar sesión, recibo 401 después de MFA" -> Relevant: session expiry, token refresh guidance.
- Topic cluster exemplar (EN): cluster that should contain only OAuth flow troubleshooting steps; cluster failure example: mix of OAuth and unrelated billing issues.

Multilingual considerations (practical checklist):
- Ensure tokenization parity across languages, record vocab coverage for each language.
- If model uses subword units, measure average token-per-span per language; large variance can bias similarity.
- Prefer native-language judgment where possible; if using translated queries, mark them as synthetic in metadata.
- Evaluate script-variant languages separately (e.g., hi vs hi-transliterated).

Operational notes and run cadence:
- Full onboarding run (automated + human annotations) should be scheduled for any candidate model before it is allowed into hosted catalog: typical wall time 3–7 business days depending on annotation queue.
- For small variants (quantized or pooling changes) a reduced fast-pass with automated metrics + 50 cluster manual checks is acceptable (48–72h).

Appendix: quick example of annotated cluster (human consensus)
- Cluster id: sample-42
- Member excerpts (3): "How to rotate API keys in console"; "Steps to revoke user tokens"; "Automated key rotation guide"
- Annotator coherence scores: 5, 4, 5 -> avg 4.7
- Tags: ["api-keys", "rotation"]
- Verdict: coherent

Next steps and owner action items:
- Run this protocol on the candidate open-model-2.0-compact (assigned: Samir Rao).
- Add scaffold to the embedding-benchmarks repo to capture pooling/normalization metadata (assigned: Elena Martínez).
- Create a follow-up ticket to implement automatic cluster example export to Confluence for easier triage (assigned: Priya Singh).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive to reduce ambiguity during model onboarding. Please comment on acceptance thresholds and any language coverage gaps.

End of doc.
